questions.explain: Only a few metals, such as iron (and steel), nickel and cobalt, are magnetic.

questions.prompt: The north pole of one magnet is brought near the north pole of another. They…
questions.explain: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.

questions.prompt: Where is a bar magnet strongest?
questions.explain: Iron filings cluster most thickly at the poles.

questions.prompt: A bar magnet is hung freely by a thread. It comes to rest pointing…
questions.explain: Earth behaves like a giant magnet, so a free magnet lines up north–south.

questions.prompt: In the Field Mapper, you place a compass beyond the magnet's N pole, along its axis. Its north end points…
questions.explain: Field lines leave the N pole, so the compass points away from it.

questions.prompt: Which things can weaken a magnet? Choose all that apply.
options: Storing it near other magnets the wrong way
Keeping it in a wooden box with keepers
questions.explain: Store magnets in pairs with keepers (soft iron pieces) to keep them strong.

questions.prompt: Plan an investigation to compare the strengths of three different magnets.
questions.modelAnswer: Independent variable: the magnet. Dependent variable: the number of identical steel paper clips each magnet can hold in a hanging chain (or the distance from which it attracts one clip, measured with a ruler). Control variables: the same size and type of paper clips, touching the same pole each time, the same method of adding clips. Repeat each test three times and average.
rubric: A measurable dependent variable (clips or distance)
questions.explain: Criterion B: plan a fair comparison.

questions.text: The region around a magnet where its force acts is its magnetic ___. A ___ is a small magnet that turns to point north–south.
questions.explain: Field lines show the direction of the magnetic field.
